([[Bel Aire, Kansas]]) | career_start = 2023 | years1 = [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2023–2024]] | team1 = [[NBA G League Ignite]] | highlights = * [[NBA G League]] Next Up Game ([[2023–24 NBA G League season|2024]]) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2023 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2023]]) * [[Jordan Brand Classic]] (2023) * [[Nike Hoop Summit]] (2022) }} '''Matas Arvidas Buzelis''' (born October 13, 2004) is a Lithuanian-American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[NBA G League Ignite]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2023 class. ==Early life and high school career== Buzelis grew up in [[Chicago|Chicago, Illinois]]. Both of his parents played basketball professionally in [[Lithuania]] before immigrating to the United States and settling in the Chicago area.{{cite web|title=UNC basketball, Hubert Davis target 5-star recruit Matas Buzelis|url=https://www.fayobserver.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2022/05/17/unc-basketball-hubert-davis-recruiting-matas-buzelis/9673176002/|work=[[The Fayetteville Observer]]|date=May 17, 2022|access-date=February 17, 2023}} In his childhood Buzelis attended [[gymnastics]] school with his brother and sister, later in the same school he attended [[Swimming (sport)|swimming]] and had the best results among under–10 and under–12 [[breaststroke]] swimmers in the [[U.S. state|state]] of [[Illinois]].{{cite web|first=Donatas|last=Urbonas|title=Buzelių DNR: už Atlanto auga įžaidėjas, kokio Lietuvoje nesutiksi|url=https://www.15min.lt/24sek/naujiena/lietuva/buzeliu-dnr-uz-atlanto-auga-izaidejas-kokio-lietuvoje-nesutiksi-875-1445756|website=[[15min.lt]]|access-date=17 August 2023|language=lt}} Buzelis initially attended [[Hinsdale Central High School]] and played on their sophomore team as a freshman.{{cite web|title=Future Illini? Hinsdale Central sophomore Matas Buzelis weighs an offer from Illinois — while waiting to play first varsity game|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/suburbs/hinsdale/sports/ct-dhd-recruiting-notes-hinsdale-central-matas-buzelis-tl-1022-20201018-jpvizepygzc2tbmb65phgfsque-story.html|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|date=October 18, 2020|access-date=February 17, 2023}} He transferred to [[Brewster Academy]], a boarding school in [[Wolfeboro, New Hampshire]], midway through the start of the first semester of his sophomore year after Hinsdale Central's basketball season was postponed due to concerns related to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-19 pandemic]].{{cite web|first=Joe|last=Henricksen|title=City/Suburban Hoops Report: The search for a No. 1 in 2023, two-sport powerhouses, prep school threats|url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/2021/11/3/22761223/high-school-basketball-asa-thomas-jj-taylor-mikey-williams|work=[[Chicago Sun-Times]]|date=November 3, 2021|access-date=February 17, 2023}} As a junior, Buzelis was named the New Hampshire Gatorade Player of the Year after averaging 11.4 points, 5.9 rebounds, 2.1 assists, 1.3 blocks, and 1.2 steals per game.{{cite press release|title=BREWSTER ACADEMY STUDENT-ATHLETE NAMED GATORADE NEW HAMPSHIRE BOYS BASKETBALL PLAYER OF THE YEAR|url=https://playeroftheyear.gatorade.com/poy/assets/writable/68460/2022_BBB_MBuzelis.pdf|date=March 16, 2022|access-date=February 17, 2023}} He was also selected to play for Team World in the 2022 [[Nike Hoops Summit]].{{cite web|first=Sam|last=Vecenie|title=Bronny James, DJ Wagner, 'JuJu' Watkins headline Nike Hoop Summit rosters|url=https://theathletic.com/4200387/2023/02/14/bronny-james-juju-watkins-nike-hoop-summit/|work=[[The Athletic]]|date=February 14, 2023|access-date=February 17, 2023}} Buzelis transferred to Sunrise Christian Academy in [[Bel Aire, Kansas]] before the start of his senior year.{{cite web|first=Eric|last=Bossi|title=Sunrise Christian has reloaded for the 2022-23 season|url=https://247sports.com/Article/College-Basketball-recruiting-Sunrise-Christian-reloads-Miro-Little-Mikel-Brown-Matas-Buzelis-Scotty-Middleton-Layden-Blocker-194856336/|work=[[247Sports]]|date=October 6, 2022|access-date=February 17, 2023}} During his senior year, he averaged 15.7 points and 5.6 rebounds per game while shooting 54 percent from the field, 42.4 percent from 3-point range and 80 percent from the free throw line.{{cite web|first=Jordan|last=Divens|title=2022-23 MaxPreps All-America Team: Cameron Boozer of Columbus headlines high school basketball's best|url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/SxUDpqUOuUW4VE3APSX7fw/2022-23-maxpreps-all-america-team-cameron-boozer-of-columbus-headlines-high-school-basketballs-best.htm|website=[[MaxPreps.com]]|date=March 29, 2023|access-date=August 5, 2023}} Buzelis was selected to play in the [[2023 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]].{{cite web|first=Daniel|last=Fair|title=Wichita basketball player named McDonald's All-American|url=https://www.ksn.com/sports/local-sports/wichita-basketball-player-named-mcdonalds-all-american/|website=[[KSN.com]]|date=January 24, 2023|access-date=February 17, 2023}} He also took part in the [[Basketball Without Borders]] camp during the [[2023 NBA All-Star Game|2023 NBA All-Star weekend]] and was named the camp's MVP.{{cite web|title=M. Buzeliui atiteko prestižinės NBA stovyklos MVP apdovanojimas|url=https://www.lrytas.lt/sportas/krepsinis/2023/02/20/news/k-kemzura-paaiskino-keista-pasirinkima-del-rintkines-kandidatu-gal-tada-deleguokime-visa-jonavos-komanda--26192234|website=[[Lrytas.lt]]|date=February 19, 2023|access-date=February 20, 2023|language=lt}} ===Recruiting=== Buzelis was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2023 class, according to major recruiting services.{{cite web|title=Kentucky, UNC, G League battle for top recruit Matas Buzelis|url=https://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/kentucky-sports/uk-recruiting/article262027972.html|work=[[Lexington Herald Leader]]|date=June 8, 2022|access-date=February 17, 2023}} He ultimately chose to play professionally for [[NBA G League Ignite]].{{cite web|first=Adrian|last=Wojnarowski|title=Sources: Five-star recruit Matas Buzelis chooses G League Ignite over college|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/34142354/sources-five-star-recruit-matas-buzelis-chooses-g-league-ignite-college|website=[[ESPN.com]]|date=June 24, 2022|access-date=February 17, 2023}}{{cite web|first=Tyler|last=Conway|title=5-Star PF Matas Buzelis Commits to G League Ignite over Kentucky, Duke, More|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10018495-5-star-pf-matas-buzelis-commits-to-g-league-ignite-over-kentucky-duke-more|work=[[Bleacher Report]]|date=June 24, 2022|access-date=February 17, 2023}} Buzelis had also considered playing [[college basketball]] for [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]], [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]], and [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest]].{{cite web|first=Andrew|last=Jones|title=UNC In Matas Buzelis' Top October 17, 2023 | bball = yes }} ==Professional career== ===NBA G League Ignite (2023–2024)=== On May 31, 2023, Buzelis officially signed with the [[NBA G League Ignite]].{{cite web|title=Matas Buzelis, projected top pick in 2024 NBA Draft, signs with G League Ignite|url=https://theathletic.com/4567760/2023/05/31/matas-buzelis-g-league-ignite/|work=[[The Athletic]]|date=May 31, Ignite|url=https://ignite.gleague.nba.com/news/mcdonalds-all-american-matas-buzelis-signs-with-ignite|website=NBA.com|date=May 31, 2023|access-date=May 31, 2023}} ==National team career== On July 21, 2022, Buzelis officially committed to the [[Lithuania men's national basketball team]] for international competitions.{{cite web|title=Five-star recruit Matas Buzelis will represent Lithuania|url=https://basketnews.com/news-175491-five-star-recruit-matas-buzelis-will-represent-lithuania.html|website=BasketNews.com|date=July 21, 2022|access-date=Jan 28, 2024}}{{cite tweet|author=LTU Basketball|title=BREAKING NEWS Matas Buzelis has committed to #LTUbasketball national teams and has been registered in FIBA system as Lithuanian.|number=1550065618258432000|user=LTU_Basketball|date=July 21, 2022|access-date=Jan 28, 2024}} ==Personal life== One of Buzelis grandfathers, Arvydas Jankauskas, is a former basketball player and coach, while his other grandfather, Petras Buzelis, also is a former basketball player who debuted in [[BC Žalgiris|Žalgiris Kaunas]] at 19 years old, later became Žalgiris Kaunas captain and won six Lithuanian League titles and three [[USSR Premier Basketball League]] bronze medals. One of Buzelis grandmothers, Elena Buzelienė, is one of the all-time greatest Lithuanian [[handball]] players who won two European Champions Cups. Buzelis's mother, Kristina Jankauskaitė, played for Lithuanian youth basketball national teams and was one of the most promising basketball players of her generation. Buzelis father, Aidas Buzelis, is a former basketball player who played for multiple [[Lietuvos krepšinio lyga|Lithuanian Basketball League]] clubs and also worked as a [[Medical massage|massage therapist]] of the [[Lithuania men's national basketball team]].{{cite web|title=Rinktinės masažuotojas – apie Kuzminsko ausis ir kūno "įjungimą"|url=https://www.delfi.lt/krepsinis/naujienos/rinktines-masazuotojas-apie-kuzminsko-ausis-ir-kuno-ijungima-82072141|work=[[DELFI]]|date=26 August 2019|access-date=17 August 2023|language=lt}} In 2022, [[Lithuanian Basketball Federation]] registered Buzelis in [[FIBA]] system as a member of the Lithuanian national team.{{cite web|title=LKF vadovai: Matas Buzelis yra pilnateisis Lietuvos rinktinės narys|url=https://www.lrt.lt/naujienos/sportas/10/1743163/lkf-vadovai-matas-buzelis-yra-pilnateisis-lietuvos-rinktines-narys|work=[[Lithuanian National Radio and Television]]|date=21 July 2022|access-date=17 August 2023|language=lt}} In 2023, Buzelis expressed his desire to play for the Lithuania men's national basketball team in the future and said that he chose it over the [[United States men's national basketball team]].{{cite web|first=Donatas|last=Urbonas|title=MVP tapęs Matas Buzelis – apie žaidimą Lietuvos rinktinėje ir galingą duetą|url=https://www.basketnews.lt/news-185403-mvp-tapes-matas-buzelis-apie-zaidima-lietuvos-rinktineje-ir-galinga-dueta.html|website=BasketNews.lt|access-date=17 August 2023|language=lt|quote=Būtų labai smagu žaisti Lietuvos rinktinėje. Aš noriu atstovauti šaliai, iš kurios kilę mano tėvai. Lietuva yra nuostabi.
